title: How Sleep Consolidates Memory
summaryZh: 睡眠不是關機，而是大腦重播並剪輯白天的經驗，留下要點、丟掉細節。

sentences.text: For most of my life I assumed sleep was simply the absence of activity, a kind of nightly power saving mode for a tired brain.
sentences.zh: 我大半輩子都以為睡眠只是活動的停止，像是疲累大腦每晚的省電模式。

sentences.text: The research of the last thirty years suggests something considerably stranger, which is that a good deal of learning happens only after you stop trying.
sentences.zh: 過去三十年的研究指出一件古怪得多的事：相當一部分的學習，是在你停止努力之後才發生的。
sentences.note: a good deal of 的 of 弱讀到幾乎只剩 /ə/；happens only 的 s 直接連到母音。

sentences.text: During the day, an experience is held in the hippocampus, a structure that is fast, flexible, and not built for permanent storage.
sentences.zh: 白天的時候，經驗被保存在海馬迴裡，那是一個快速、有彈性，卻不是為長期儲存而設計的結構。

sentences.text: At night, particularly in deep slow wave sleep, those patterns are replayed to the cortex at something like ten times the original speed.
sentences.zh: 到了夜裡，尤其是在深層的慢波睡眠中，這些模式會以大約十倍的速度重播給大腦皮質。

sentences.text: Researchers can actually see this in rats, where the sequence of cells that fired along a maze fires again, compressed, in the same order.
sentences.zh: 研究者在老鼠身上真的看得到：牠跑迷宮時依序放電的細胞，會以壓縮的形式、依同樣順序再放一次。

sentences.text: What makes the finding interesting is not the replay itself, but what appears to get left out of it.
sentences.zh: 這個發現真正有意思的地方，不在於重播本身，而在於重播時似乎被略過的東西。
sentences.note: not 和 but 之間是典型的對比句型，not 要重讀，but 之後語調重新拉高。

sentences.text: The brain does not archive the day faithfully, and anyone who has tried to recall a Tuesday from last March already knows this.
sentences.zh: 大腦並不會忠實地把一天存檔，任何試著回想去年三月某個星期二的人都已經知道這件事。

sentences.text: It seems to keep the gist and discard the surface, which is why you remember the argument and not the exact words that started it.
sentences.zh: 它似乎保留大意、丟掉表層，所以你記得那場爭執，卻記不得引爆爭執的確切字句。
sentences.note: keep the 的 p 在 th 前不爆破；the exact 的 the 唸成 /ði/，連成 /ði.ɪɡ.ˈzækt/。

sentences.text: There is a cost to that, of course, since a memory rebuilt from gist is a memory that can quietly go wrong.
sentences.zh: 當然這是有代價的，因為從大意重建出來的記憶，是一種可能悄悄出錯的記憶。

sentences.text: I find it useful to think of the whole process as editing rather than recording, though I'd hold that metaphor loosely.
sentences.zh: 我覺得把整個過程想成剪輯而不是錄影很有幫助，不過這個比喻我不會抓得太死。
sentences.note: find it 連成 /ˈfaɪn.dɪt/；editing 和 recording 是一組對比重音，必須拉出來。

sentences.text: The practical implications are less dramatic than the headlines suggest, and I want to be careful not to oversell them here.
sentences.zh: 實際的意義沒有新聞標題講得那麼戲劇化，我也想小心不要在這裡誇大。

sentences.text: Cutting sleep short does not simply make you tired the next day; it appears to remove the window in which the day was going to be filed.
sentences.zh: 睡眠不足不只是讓你隔天疲倦；它似乎直接拿走了那段用來把這一天歸檔的時間。
sentences.note: 分號前後是一組對比：not simply tired 對上 remove the window，兩邊重音都要拉出來。

sentences.text: A student who studies until three in the morning has traded the very hours that would have turned the studying into knowledge.
sentences.zh: 熬夜念到凌晨三點的學生，交換掉的正是那幾個能把念過的內容變成知識的小時。

sentences.text: That is a real finding, and it is also the kind of finding that gets repeated until it sounds like a slogan.
sentences.zh: 那是一個真實的研究結果，但它也是那種被重複到聽起來像口號的結果。

sentences.text: What I take from it is narrower and, I think, harder to argue with: the work of learning is not finished when you stop working.
sentences.zh: 我從中得到的結論比較窄，但我想也比較難反駁：學習這件事，不會在你停止用功的那一刻結束。
sentences.note: narrower 和 harder 是並列重音；冒號後語調重新起頭，像是把結論端出來。

questions.q: According to the writer, what happens during deep slow wave sleep?
options: The brain shuts down almost completely to save energy
Daytime patterns are replayed to the cortex at high speed
New experiences are recorded exactly as they happened

questions.q: Why does the writer prefer the word editing to the word recording?
options: Because sleep erases most memories entirely
Because the brain keeps the gist and drops the surface detail
Because memories stay in the hippocampus permanently

questions.q: What is the writer's attitude toward the practical advice drawn from this research?
options: He thinks popular coverage overstates it
He believes it should be taught in every school
He doubts the underlying research is sound
